discovery: Quantum key distribution: the invention of quantum cryptography based on single-photon states and entanglement

nominees.name: Charles H. Bennett
nominees.affiliation: IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center, Yorktown Heights, USA

nominees.name: Artur Ekert
nominees.affiliation: University of Oxford, UK, and Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore

motivation: Bennett and Brassard (BB84) showed that the laws of quantum physics, namely the no-cloning property and the disturbance caused by measuring incompatible observables, can guarantee the secrecy of a shared key. Their 1989 experiment was the first demonstration. Ekert (1991) independently linked key security to entanglement and to the violation of Bell inequalities, so that a foundational test became a cryptographic resource. This later led to device-independent protocols. Together these ideas founded quantum information science as an experimental discipline. They gave rise to fibre and satellite QKD networks, continuous-variable variants and a whole field of quantum communication technology. Measuring incompatible observables in different contexts turned out to be a physical resource, not a paradox. In this way quantum foundations became a practical device, a transformation that the Nobel Prize should recognise.
